France 20: 157 (1873) | range_map = | range_map_caption = }} '''''Camptotheca acuminata''''' is a species of [[tree]] in the genus ''[[Camptotheca]]'' that is native to north [[Vietnam]] and southern [[China]].{{Cite web |title=Camptotheca acuminata Decne. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:271482-1 |access-date=2024-09-13 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}} It is also cultivated in the southern United States.{{Cite book |last1=Lewis |first1=Walter H. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ipQmSriMF9sC&pg=PA205 |title=Medical Botany: Plants Affecting Human Health |last2=Elvin-Lewis |first2=Memory P. F. |date=2003-09-04 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-0-471-62882-8 |pages=205–206 |language=en}} A [[eudicot]],{{Cite web |title=Camptotheca acuminata |url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/taxonomy/16922/ |access-date=2024-09-13 |website=NCBI |language=en}} it is a flowering [[deciduous]] tree with light gray bark.{{Cite WFO|title=Camptotheca acuminata|id=0000794374}} It can grow to a height of {{convert|20|m|ft}}. Its large, papery leaves are somewhat oval in shape, usually {{convert|12|to|28|cm|abbr=on|sigfig=1|in}} long and {{convert|6|to|12|cm|abbr=on|sigfig=1|in}} wide. The flowers, which bloom from May through July, produce a gray-brown fruit with one seed in September. ==Uses== ''Camptotheca acuminata'' is a source of [[camptothecin]] chemicals, which have been tested for potential use as treatments for cancer and HIV. The modern [[chemotherapy]] drugs [[topotecan]] and [[irinotecan]] are derived from it, though now the molecules are produced in a lab environment rather than extracted from the leaves and bark of the tree.{{Cite book |last1=Foster |first1=Steven |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mE0z2MnIsloC&pg=PA202 |title=National Geographic Desk Reference to Nature's Medicine |last2=Johnson |first2=Rebecca L. |date=2008 |publisher=National Geographic Books |isbn=978-1-4262-0293-3 |pages=202–203 |language=en}} Because of this, it is sometimes called the "cancer tree". In [[traditional Chinese medicine]], the tree is called '''xǐ shù''' ([[Simplified Chinese]]:'''喜树''') and was considered a relatively unimportant [[medicinal plant]].
